text:
Made some updates to the Alphaport iOS app (coming for android soon). Also now available in Europe. Try it out here: https://t.co/Wi7eqomKfe

I added some basic functionality for users who don't have an account but still want to look up information about companies. The experience is much better if you're a desktop user as well though.

How am i personally using the app? Well,
1. The app will send you notifications each day when 13f filers have positions that are below their estimated cost basis. So, for example you might think $ISRG is expensive (I do) but its interesting that Coatue almost certainly paid more than you would be paying.
2. Quick glance at the feed in the morning is the most efficient way to get up to speed on basic factors etc.
3. This is the easiest way to see 'competitor read through' earnings calls - none of my companies are reporting atm (well, $FLWS which i was short gg no re), but you can see $ZS reported which affects $CRWD and $QLYS which i am short, for example.
4. quick way to view your sector weightings, something that is annoying to check in IB etc. For example, I am quite a bit more long financials than i thought, has just slowly crept up. Nothing crazy but interesting to know.

This is my investing journal, shared for entertainment - not financial advice.

This week I achieved all time highs once again with strong performance outside the AI theme. Feels good.

Perhaps just as important, the portfolio has become quite diversified despite my view that the AI trade still represents the best value in the market (but with increasing levels of tail risk). Interestingly, I am now more overweight healthcare/biotech than the AI trade, with the AI segment totalling 34% of net, but healthcare sector exposure at 40% of net.  I have mostly stuck to diagnostics on the bios side though I'm increasingly looking wider. Clinical just takes a long time to ramp. For example, I've tried to really get my head around $INSM 3 times, and i still dont fully have it down cold.

The combination requires relentless work. Most days I am raising the bar on the type of data available on ALPHAPORT (for example, easily accessible segment and product data has helped understand semicap companies, like $MKSI, better). This has actually helped quite a bit - spend enough time breaking down semicap service revenue and you sort of start to know the sector cold, which is the goal. Try to understand the business as well as the CEO. It's impossible, but you try.

On top of compute/biotech, I've continued trying to build smaller positions across aerospace and defense, with $079550 (LIG) starting to work out ok (they make a surface to air missile that is 1/3 the cost of the patriot), $IA still chugging along, and a new starter position in $BUKS. BUKS is just small for now. The financials are good, but I haven't fully dialed in the details here yet. I've also increased $FTAI steadily. A lot of people see this as a power generation play with AI data center exposure, but the details of their aerospace business show a company that is executing very well. On my 'maybe?' list is $KTOS, though $FTAI seems strictly better to me.

This week i've really worked to avoid spending too much time watching numbers go up and down on a screen and try to focus my attentions on understanding the quite difficult to understand details of these fairly technical industries. Basically - what is going to happen? What can I learn so that I have a more differentiated insight into figuring out, what the hell are they building in there?

So far it seems like my viewpoint has been good - the AI bio theme continues to provide a major tailwind to previously undervalued diagnostics companies, a theme I talked about in detail here: https://t.co/r3WdpVkryr.

I have avoided too much trading in and out of the compute theme despite incredible amounts of fud coming on a weekly basis. Often this means figuring out what the effect of something like Kimi Delta Attention or TypeSafe will be will be in less than 24 hours, only to then decide 'eh, it'll probably be fine'.

Overall, September has gone well so far. Lets hope we close out the rest of the year strong.

Feel free to ask any questions in the thread,

Martin
